name: YASA v0.8.0 wearable evaluation module
org: YASA (raphaelvallat/yasa, open source sleep analysis toolbox)
role: Raphael Vallat, creator and core maintainer
why: YASA is a widely used open source Python toolbox for sleep analysis. Its October 2026 release adds EpochByEpochAgreement and SleepStatsAgreement, a module built to compare a wearable or sleep staging algorithm against a reference. That is the exact workflow a new overnight band needs to show its sleep timing honestly, and a worked wearable example would help its users.
why_now: v0.8.0 shipped 2 Oct 2026 (PyPI and GitHub releases) with the new evaluation module; v0.7.0 followed in March 2026 with the Hypnogram class. The project runs active GitHub Discussions in 2026.
channel: GitHub Discussions (Show and tell / ideas); maintainer email on PyPI (raphaelvallat9@gmail.com)
warm_path: Post in YASA Discussions once a sample overnight file exists; the maintainer answers there publicly.
ask: Would a wearable example (band derived hypnogram vs reference) be welcome as a tutorial or discussion post once our sample nights exist?
opener: Hi Raphael, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK. The new evaluation module in YASA v0.8.0 is the workflow we want to follow when we check our sleep timing against a reference. Once ready, I'd be glad to share our SDK docs and some sample overnight data in whatever shape fits EpochByEpochAgreement. Would a short wearable example posted in Discussions be useful to your users, or is there a format you'd prefer?
opportunity: Use YASA's wearable evaluation module on Vybe sample nights and offer a public worked example to the maintainer.

name: GGIR and GGIRread device file readers
org: wadpac (GGIR / GGIRread, open source R toolkit for wearable sensor data)
role: Vincent T van Hees, maintainer (per CRAN)
why: GGIR is a standard R toolkit for sleep and activity research from wrist sensors, and GGIRread holds its device readers. Readers already cover GENEActiv, Axivity, ActiGraph, Actical, Actiwatch, Fitbit (including heart rate) and Philips Health Band epoch exports, and the September 2026 release includes code contributed by a device manufacturer. A reader for a new band's epoch export is the kind of contribution the project already takes.
why_now: GGIRread 1.0.11 released 18 Sep 2026 with a GENEActiv change contributed by ActivInsights Ltd, the device maker; GGIR 3.3-9 published on CRAN 12 Sep 2026.
channel: GitHub issue on wadpac/GGIRread; maintainer email listed on CRAN (v.vanhees@accelting.com)
warm_path: Open a GitHub issue proposing a reader for Vybe's epoch export, following the pattern of the Fitbit and Philips Health Band readers.
ask: Would you accept a reader for our band's overnight epoch export (heart rate plus sleep timing) if we open an issue with a sample file and format spec?
opener: Hi Vincent, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK. I saw GGIRread 1.0.11 in September included a change contributed by ActivInsights, and that the Fitbit reader now loads heart rate. Once ready, I'd like to share our SDK docs, a format spec and sample overnight files so researchers can read our epoch exports in GGIR. Would an issue with a sample file be the right first step, or do you prefer another route?
opportunity: Contribute a GGIRread reader for Vybe epoch exports so sleep researchers using GGIR can analyse Vybe nights.

name: OxWearables actipy and asleep
org: Oxford Wearables Group (OxWearables, University of Oxford)
role: Maintainers of actipy and asleep (GitHub OxWearables)
why: actipy reads raw wrist sensor files (Axivity, ActiGraph, GENEActiv, Matrix, plus generic CSV) and asleep estimates sleep timing and stages from wrist data, trained on over 1,000 nights of multi centre reference recordings. Both welcome bug reports, feature requests and pull requests. If our band's motion stream fits their CSV path, Vybe nights could run through a well known open pipeline.
why_now: actipy 3.8.3 released 30 Sep 2026 with hardened device parsers; asleep 0.5.0 published on PyPI 9 Oct 2026.
channel: GitHub Discussions on OxWearables/asleep; GitHub issues on actipy
warm_path: Open a feature request on actipy describing the export format once a sample file exists.
ask: Would a device reader for our band's export be welcome in actipy, or should we target the generic CSV path for asleep?
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK. I noticed actipy 3.8.3 hardened the device parsers in September and asleep 0.5.0 landed in October. Once ready, I'd be glad to share our SDK docs and sample overnight files so you can see whether our motion data suits asleep. Would you rather we propose a dedicated reader in actipy, or start with the generic CSV route?
opportunity: Get Vybe exports readable by actipy and asleep so Oxford's open sleep pipeline can run on Vybe nights.

name: JupyterHealth omh-shim (adding a new source)
why: omh-shim converts wearable data from device makers' own schemas to IEEE 1752 and Open mHealth schemas for JupyterHealth Exchange, and ships a step by step guide titled Adding a New Source for new devices. Heart rate and sleep duration converters already exist for Oura and Open Wearables, so a Vybe source would slot into an existing pattern.
why_now: v2.1.0 released 19 Sep 2026 (CHANGELOG and PyPI) with new sleep converters; docs/adding-a-source.md invites new device sources.
warm_path: Open an issue proposing a Vybe source module, referencing the Adding a New Source guide.
ask: Would you accept a Vybe source module for heart rate, HRV and sleep episodes if we follow your Adding a New Source guide?
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health. Once ready, I'd like to share our SDK docs and sample overnight records so we can write converters with test fixtures in your format. Which data types would you most want covered first for JupyterHealth users?
opportunity: Add Vybe as an omh-shim source so its nights convert to IEEE 1752 and Open mHealth for JupyterHealth Exchange.

why_now: Version 0.17.18 released 3 Sep 2026 after 0.17.16 and 0.17.17 in late August 2026 (GitHub releases).
channel: GitHub issue on pfizer-opensource/scikit-digital-health; author email on PyPI (lukas.adamowicz@pfizer.com)
warm_path: Open a GitHub issue asking whether a new reader is in scope, with a sample file attached once available.

opener: Hi Lukas, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health.
